mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays elevated or rebounds, commuter foot traffic expands weekday shopping trips and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if work mobility keeps falling while retail still rises.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days than over the prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES holding flat or rising for at least two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed rise in GROCERY_PHARM pulls household errand clustering toward nearby commercial strips, which raises RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. The effect fails if grocery mobility rises without any pickup in retail visits.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns up by at least 2 points week-on-week after a flat or declining month
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM posts a week-on-week gain of 2 or more points.

mechanism_narrative: A joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates more commuting and city-center circulation, which should push RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks. The signal fails when transit weakens even as workplaces rise.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are above their current week means relative to the prior two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL is above baseline and PARKS falls at the same time, discretionary outside-home leisure shifts away from shopping districts, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails if residents stay home more but retail visits still rise.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains positive and PARKS remains negative versus baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in PARKS signals weather or seasonality that suppresses discretionary shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should fall in the next one to four weeks. The signal fails if park mobility drops but retail does not weaken.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by 5 or more points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after PARKS posts a week-on-week drop of at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply depressed at the same time, the city is still operating under weak mobility restrictions and retail demand stays below its recent four-week average. The mechanism fails once transit and workplaces recover together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 and WORKPLACES remains below -15 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -40 and WORKPLACES stays below -15 for two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lag rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after a prior dip captures renewed household movement that spills into nearby retail districts, producing higher RETAIL_REC within one week. The effect fails if grocery activity recovers but retail remains flat.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises after a two-week decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM reverses upward from a two-week decline.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL eases while TRANSIT improves, more residents leave home for mixed-purpose outings, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The signal fails when residential mobility stays elevated and transit does not recover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL declines and TRANSIT rises relative to the current week.
